initial_prompt: My dog just died. I feel like I can't breathe. I don't know what to do.

messages.content: My dog just died. I feel like I can't breathe. I don't know what to do.

I am so incredibly sorry. Losing a dog is a profound, shattering loss. They are our family, our shadows, and our purest sources of love. It makes perfect sense that you feel like you can't breathe right now; your body is reacting to the sudden physical absence of a huge part of your life.

Please, try to be gentle with yourself in this exact moment. You are in shock. The feeling of suffocation is a panic response to grief, and while it feels terrifying, it will pass. Just try to focus on taking one slow breath, then another. You do not need to figure out the next hour, or even the next ten minutes. You just need to get through this minute.

If you are currently with your dog, please know that there is no rush. You don't have to call anyone or move them right this second. It is okay to just sit with them, to pet them, or to cry. If it feels too hard to look at them, it is okay to cover them with a blanket. Do whatever your heart needs you to do to feel safe.

If you have a friend or family member who understands how much your dog meant to you, please call them. You don't need to explain anything or ask them to do anything—just having another voice on the line can help ground you so you aren't sitting in the silence alone.

You are going through a trauma right now. Let the tears come. Whatever you are feeling is the right thing to feel.
